name: SBA Communications Corporation
executive_summary: SBA Communications is a US-listed tower REIT owning 46,328 sites (FY2025 10-K), with site leasing contributing 97.9% of segment operating profit. The quantitative screen flags a buy on cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk factors (P/E 18.4, yield 2.9%, Neff PEGY 0.07, Piotroski and earnings-quality passes). The investment case rests on recurring, escalator-linked lease revenue, strong operating margins, and capital return via dividends and buybacks, set against a leveraged balance sheet and elevated churn from carrier consolidation and network exits. Valuation looks reasonable for a high-quality infrastructure compounder, but negative book equity and ~$13bn of debt limit margin of safety. The central debate is whether organic growth and Millicom-driven international scale can offset Sprint/EchoStar churn and rising interest expense in a higher-rate refinancing cycle.
investment_thesis:
For a value-oriented investor, SBAC offers exposure to essential wireless infrastructure with contractually recurring revenue, long ground-lease tenure (average remaining life ~35 years including renewals under control, per FY2025 10-K), and a capital-light incremental-tenant model (1.8 tenants per site). The screen’s buy signal aligns with business quality: six models pass across five factor families, data quality is high (18/20 metrics), and conviction is persistent at 56%. Filings describe a REIT structure (since 2016) that shields most US tower cash flow from corporate tax, with dividends ($1.25/share quarterly in Q1 2026 10-Q) and repurchases ($1.5bn authorisation, $1.1bn remaining per Q1 2026 10-Q) as explicit capital-allocation tools.

The value hook is not deep distress but relative cheapness on earnings and cash yield versus infrastructure peers, with net income and site-leasing revenue trending up despite identifiable churn. FY2025 net income rose materially year-on-year (Yahoo fallback: $1.05bn vs $0.75bn in 2024), and interim filings show continued top-line growth: Q1 2026 total revenue was $703.4m (+5.9% YoY per Q1 2026 10-Q). Site development remains cyclical and small (~7% of revenue in Q1 2026), reinforcing the quality of the core leasing franchise. Negative P/B (-3.9 on screen) reflects accumulated deficits from buybacks and dividends against negative GAAP equity—not a traditional asset bargain, but consistent with levered REIT capital structures.
financial_review:
**Annual results (10-K)**  
Two annual 10-K filings are indexed (FY2024 filed Feb 2025; FY2025 filed Feb 2026). Body extracts are truncated at 80,000 characters and contain business, risk, and MD&A narrative but **not** consolidated income statements, balance sheets, or cash-flow statements. Annual line-item figures below therefore fall back to Yahoo `financials_annual.json`; narrative metrics are from filing bodies.

| Metric | FY2025 (Yahoo) | FY2024 (Yahoo) | FY2023 (Yahoo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total revenue | $2,815.1m | $2,679.6m | $2,711.6m |
| Operating income | $1,554.3m | $1,569.6m | $1,114.7m |
| Net income | $1,053.6m | $749.5m | $501.8m |
| Diluted EPS | $9.80 | $6.94 | $4.61 |
| EBITDA (reported) | $2,011.1m | $1,470.0m | $1,701.1m |
| Free cash flow | $1,066.5m | $1,106.7m | $1,307.7m |

FY2025 revenue grew ~5% YoY; net income rose ~41%, aided by lower unusual/impairment charges versus 2024 (Yahoo shows $211m unusual items in 2025 vs $140m in 2024). Operating income was broadly flat, with higher D&A and interest offsetting revenue growth.

From the FY2025 10-K narrative (filing body): total **principal indebtedness** was **$12,959.8m** and **shareholders’ deficit** was **$4,853.5m** at 31 Dec 2025 (vs $13,672.8m debt and $5,109.9m deficit at 31 Dec 2024). Variable-rate debt was ~$2.7bn (21.1% of total). Customer concentration remains high: T-Mobile 31.1%, AT&T 20.3%, Verizon 15.1% of total revenue in 2025. The company purchased 7,000+ Millicom sites in Central America during 2025 and exited/sold Philippines, Colombia, and substantially all of Canada.

**Interim results (10-Q)**  
Six interim 10-Q filings are indexed with bodies available; trends below are from filing extracts.

**Q1 2026 (Mar 2026 10-Q):** Total revenue **$703.4m** (+5.9% YoY); site leasing **$656.1m** (+6.5%); operating income **$342.8m**; net income attributable **$184.8m**; diluted EPS **$1.74** (vs $2.04 in Q1 2025). Interest expense **$128.5m** (+23% YoY). Operating cash flow **$255.1m** (vs $301.2m prior year). Total debt principal **$13,014m** at 31 Mar 2026; current maturities **$2,684m** reflect near-term refinancing activity (e.g. $750m Tower Securities repaid Jan 2026, revolver drawn).

**Nine months ended Sep 2025 (Sep 2025 10-Q):** Total revenue **$2,095.6m** (+5.5% YoY); net income attributable **$683.3m** (+18.7%); diluted EPS **$6.34** (vs $5.33). YTD operating cash flow **$987.3m**; capex **$162.1m**; acquisitions **$664.4m**.

**Q3 2025:** Revenue **$732.3m**; net income attributable **$236.8m**; diluted EPS **$2.20**.

**Trend assessment:** Site-leasing revenue is growing, driven by organic leases/amendments, Millicom towers, and escalators, partially offset by domestic churn (Sprint, EchoStar). Operating income is resilient but net income is pressured by higher interest expense (refinancing lower-rate secured paper into revolver/term loan at higher blended rates, per Q1 2026 MD&A). Asset impairment and decommission costs remain meaningful ($29.3m in Q1 2026; $102.6m in 9M 2025), linked to churn-driven tower rationalisation. FCF remains positive at the annual level (Yahoo: $1.07bn FY2025) but is consumed by dividends (~$479m), buybacks (~$498m), acquisitions (~$1.06bn), and net debt reduction.

**Gap note:** Full-year GAAP statement tables are absent from truncated 10-K body extracts; verify annual figures against full EDGAR HTML before trading.
risks_and_flags:
**Leverage and covenants.** Substantial indebtedness (~$13bn) and negative equity are structural features, not one-offs. FY2025 10-K discloses Senior Credit Agreement covenants: Consolidated Net Debt / Annualised Borrower EBITDA ≤ **6.5×**; Annualised Borrower EBITDA / Annualised Cash Interest Expense ≥ **2.0×** (SBA Senior Finance II was in compliance at 31 Mar 2026 per Q1 2026 10-Q). Tower Securities borrowers must maintain debt service coverage ≥ **1.30×**; failure triggers cash trapping and potential amortisation below **1.15×**. Restrictive covenants limit M&A, dividends, and asset sales. No “going concern” or “substantial doubt” language appears in available filing bodies.

**Churn and customer credit.** Management guides **$132–136m** of domestic cash site-leasing churn in 2026 (Sprint and EchoStar) and **$36–40m** internationally (Oi wireline), per Q1 2026 MD&A. Sprint/T-Mobile overlap churn is expected to total ~**$75m** over several years (FY2025 10-K). EchoStar (f/k/a DISH Wireless) notified discontinuation of its network; it **defaulted on payment obligations in Dec 2025**, with ~**$56m** of 2026 revenue at risk (FY2025 10-K). Customer concentration in three US carriers (~66% of revenue) amplifies carrier capex and credit cycles.

**Interest-rate and refinancing risk.** ~21% of debt is variable-rate; swaps cover $2.0bn of the term loan at 5.165% through Apr 2028. Q1 2026 interest expense rose 23% YoY as lower-rate secured notes were repaid with revolver borrowings at ~4.8%. Refinancing maturities are elevated: **$2.68bn** current debt at 31 Mar 2026.

**International and FX.** ~25% of FY2025 revenue from international operations; Brazil, Guatemala, and Central America are material. FX remeasurement of intercompany loans caused volatile other income ($81.6m gain in 2025 vs $156.8m loss in 2024 per FY2025 10-K). Brazil tax assessments are under appeal; Q1 2026 10-Q cites reasonably possible loss range of **$0–$114.1m** (excluding penalties/interest of $184.4m).

**Competitive and technology.** Competes with American Tower, Crown Castle, carrier-owned towers, and alternatives (DAS, small cells, satellite). FY2025 10-K warns that network sharing, small cells, and technology shifts could reduce tower demand; SBAC’s portfolio is less diversified into small cells than some peers.

**Governance / pension.** No material pension obligations flagged in reviewed extracts. Annual meeting (8-K, 23 May 2025) re-elected directors and approved executive compensation; no management change flagged in reviewed news.

research_rationale: Deep research broadly confirms the screen’s buy case on earnings yield, dividend growth, and franchise quality, but tempers conviction owing to leverage, identifiable 2026 churn, and rising interest expense that truncated annual filings do not fully quantify.
